title: Veterans Pension Net Worth, Asset Transfers and the Penalty Period
content:
# Net worth and asset transfers under Veterans Pension

## 1. Net worth limit

No Veterans Pension is payable while net worth — assets other than the primary residence and a residential lot of up to the product's excluded acreage (2 acres), plus annual countable income — exceeds the product's net worth limit. An award whose net worth rises above the limit is terminated for excess net worth, and the veteran may reapply once net worth is at or below it.

## 2. Which transfers are penalized — the look-back

A transfer is penalized only when the date of the asset transfer is not more than 36 calendar months before the date VA receives the claim or the report of the transfer. Add the look-back months to the transfer date; when the resulting month has no such day, use the last day of that month, and a report received on that date is still within the look-back period.

The clock starts on the transfer date shown on the report; the comparison is against the date VA received the claim or the report of that same transfer; the end date is inside the period.

| Transfer date | End of look-back | Claim or report received | Penalized |
|---|---|---|---|
| May 31, 2022 | May 31, 2025 | May 31, 2025 | Yes |
| May 31, 2022 | May 31, 2025 | June 1, 2025 | No |
| February 29, 2024 | February 28, 2027 | February 28, 2027 | Yes |

## 3. Covered amount and penalty period

The covered amount is the part of the uncompensated transfer that would have put net worth above the limit: the lesser of the amount transferred and the amount by which net worth plus the amount transferred exceeds the limit, and never below zero. The penalty period is the covered amount divided by the product's monthly penalty rate, rounded down to whole months, never more than the product's longest penalty period, and it starts the first day of the month after the month of the last transfer. No pension is paid during the penalty period. A transfer to a trust for a child who cannot self-support is not penalized.

### Worked example (hypothetical, using the product figures 163699, 2873 and 60)

A veteran's net worth is 150000.00 after giving 30000.00 to a relative in March. Net worth plus the transfer is 180000.00, which exceeds 163699 by 16301.00; that is less than the 30000.00 transferred, so the covered amount is 16301.00. Divided by 2873 it is 5.67, rounded down to 5 months, starting April 1. Had net worth after the gift been 120000.00, net worth plus the transfer (150000.00) would not exceed the limit and the covered amount would be zero.
